samples.summary: No test ties the `outcome=` values the gate step writes to the `case` labels the loop-status step reads — a rename in either place silently degrades to the "cancelled, killed, or never ran" note, the exact mis-attribution this delta exists to fix
samples.evidence: The delta introduces two independent literal sets: the writers at agent-review-panel.yml:1517/1527/1528/1530/1533/1535 (`promoted`, `crashed`, `gates-unsatisfied`, `tooling-error`, `flip-failed`, `unhandled-status`) and the readers at :1564-1569. Nothing checks they agree. The one YAML test over this block, mark-ready.test.mjs:424 ("agent-review-panel.yml handles every mark-ready code, defaults the rest"), enumerates the `case "$code"` branch labels and their `exit` statuses (lines 461-498) and asserts only `ready=true` for branch 0 (line 481) — it never mentions `outcome`, so deleting every `echo "outcome=..."` line, or misspelling one, keeps the whole suite green while every non-promotion reports "the gate did not reach a decision — it was cancelled, killed, or never ran". The repo already has precedent for exactly this kind of two-sites-must-agree YAML assertion (checks.test.mjs:168-199 evaluates the gate `if:` against the concurrency partition; mark-ready.test.mjs:500-509 pins the grep needle across files), so the pattern was available and was not applied here. Also unasserted: that each `outcome=` write precedes its branch's `exit` (the comment at :1513-1514 states this as the load-bearing property).

samples.summary: set-state's CI signal was switched to the new path-matched, all-runs-must-be-green `ciConclusion`, and nothing tests `gatherSignals` at any level
samples.evidence: set-state.mjs:226-229 now calls `ciConclusion(runs)` instead of the inline newest-name-match. set-state.test.mjs contains only pure-helper tests (labelFor/computeLabelSet/isValidTransition/deriveState/sameLabelSet — see the `test(` census at lines 14-118); `deriveState` is fed a literal `ciConclusion` string (lines 83-99), so it cannot observe how the signal is derived. There is no process-level stub-`gh` harness for set-state as there is for mark-ready. Consequence if the derivation is wrong (e.g. runs arriving without `path`, or the path constant drifting): `sig.ciConclusion` becomes null for every PR, `deriveState` returns `awaiting-ci` for a green draft, and the lifecycle label is wrong with no test failing. checks.test.mjs covers `ciConclusion` in isolation but nothing covers set-state's call site or the field-shape assumption (`path` present on the `actions/runs` response objects).
searchedFor: glob for other set-state test files

samples.summary: ciConclusion tests cover only success/failure/null conclusions — the terminal non-success values GitHub actually emits (cancelled, skipped, neutral, timed_out, action_required) are untested
